correctness.rationale: Unit-radius 600-cell vertices are 8 coordinate, 16 half-sign, and 96 even-permutation golden coordinates. Writing doubled coordinates in Z[phi], 36 V^2=det(X^tX), and the cubic Gram determinant is (A+B phi)/64, so V^2=(A+B phi)/2304. Independent full anchored enumeration of all C(119,3)=273819 triples found 164 distinct exact pairs, zero count 2419, maximum (160,256) with 20 anchored and next (160,240) with 120; transitivity times 30 yields 600 and 3600, and 72570 degenerate tetrahedra. Actual SPECTRUM.csv has exactly 164 rows, sum 8214570 and matching extrema/zeros; verifier independently checks Cauchy–Binet and all rows. The maximum regular golden-edge tetrahedra have 600 cliques with 720 edges and 1200 triangles. Coordinatewise convexity of the exterior-product norm puts some maximum of any four contained points at vertices. No assertion of exclusive nonvertex equality.
